questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A TV transmission tower of height $h$ covers a range of distance $d$. By how much will be the range change, if the height is increased to $3 / 2 \mathrm{~h} ?$
questions.solution:
If a tower of height $h$ covers a range of distance $d$, then $d=\sqrt{2 h R}$. where, $R$ is the radius of the earth. when $h^{\prime}=\frac{3}{2} h$, then $d^{\prime}=\sqrt{2 h^{\prime} R^{\prime}}$
$=\sqrt{2 \times \frac{3}{2} h R}=\sqrt{\frac{3}{2} d}$
$\therefore$ The range of distance will change by
$\Delta d=d^{\prime}-d=\left(\sqrt{\frac{3}{2}}-1\right) d$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Identify the logic gate for which the output is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo></math> when any of the inputs is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn></math>
questions.solution:
For NOR gate, truth table is given by, Y=A+B.

So if any one of the input is 1, then output will be zero.

For NAND gate, truth table is given by, Y=AB, so for any input 1, output will be 1.

For AND gate, truth table is given by, Y=AB, so for any one input 1, output may be 0 or 1.

For OR gate, truth table is given by, Y=A+B, so for any one output 1, output will be 0 or 1.

questions.q: If the temperature of the semi-conductor is increased, which of the following is correct statement?
options: The number of electrons in valence band increases
The number of electrons in conduction band increases
The number of holes in valence band decreases
questions.solution: In the case of semiconductors, resistivity is inversely proportional to the temperature. In this case as temperature increases, electrons jump to conduction band resistance decreases. So resistivity also decreases and current increases. The vibration of electrons increases with rising in temperature and hence collision between ions and electrons increases with temperature. So the number of electrons in the conduction band increases.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The modulation index used in amplitude modulation of a message signal of peak voltage $10 \mathrm{~V}$ is 0.5 . By how much the peak voltage of the carrier signal be changed, so as to obtain the modulation index of 0.8 , keeping the peak voltage of the message signal same as before?
questions.solution:
Initially modulation index, $\mu=0.5$ and
message amplitude, $A_m=10 \mathrm{~V}$
As,
$\mu=\frac{A_m}{A_c} \Rightarrow A_{c_1}=\frac{A_m}{\mu}=\frac{10}{0.5}=20 \mathrm{~V}$
When $\mu=0.8$ and $A_m=10 \mathrm{~V}$,
$A_{c_2}=\frac{A_m}{\mu}=\frac{10}{0.8}=12.5 \mathrm{~V}$
Change in carrier amplitude is
$\Delta A_c=A_{c_1}-A_{c_2}=20-12.5=7.5 \mathrm{~V}$
Thus, carrier frequency is reduced by $7.5 \mathrm{~V}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: The resistance of intrinsic semiconductors decrease with increase of temperature

Doping pure <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>S</mi><mi>i</mi></math> with trivalent impurities give <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>p</mi></math>-type semiconductors
The majority carriers in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>n</mi></math>-type semiconductors are holes
A <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>p</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>n</mi></math> junction can act as a semiconductor device
questions.solution:
The resistance of intrinsic semiconductors decreases with the increase of temperature. Doping pure Si with trivalent impurities gives p-type semiconductors. A p-n junction can act as a semiconductor device.

The majority of carriers in n-type semiconductors are electrons, not holes. Atoms got a greater amount of electrons in the conduction band of a n-type semiconductor, i.e. doped with a pentavalent impurity, in comparison to the number of holes in the valence band.

questions.q: A message signal is used to modulated a carrier signal of frequency $5 \mathrm{MHz}$ and peak voltage of $40 \mathrm{~V}$. In the process, two side-bands are produced seperated by $40 \mathrm{kHz}$. If the modulation index is 0.75 , then the peak voltage and frequency of the messages signal, respectively are
questions.solution:
Given, frequency of carrier signal, $f=5 \mathrm{MHz}$
and peak voltage, $V_c=40 \mathrm{~V}$
Modulation index, $\mu=0.75\therefore \quad \mu=\frac{V_m}{V_c} \quad \begin{array}{r}{\left[\because V_m \text { is peak voltage }\right.} \\ \text { of message signal }]\end{array}\begin{aligned} 0.75 & =\frac{V_m}{40} \\ \Rightarrow \quad V_m & =40 \times 0.75 \\ V_m & =30 \mathrm{~V}\end{aligned}$
Since, difference of frequencies of two side bands is equal to the band width ( $2 \mathrm{fm})$.
i.e., Band width $=40 \mathrm{kHz}2 f_{\mathrm{m}}=40 \mathrm{kHz} \Rightarrow f_{\mathrm{m}}=20 \mathrm{kHz}$
Hence, the peak voltage and frequencey will be $30 \mathrm{~V}$ and $20 \mathrm{kHz}$.

questions.q: A transmitting antenna has a height $20 \mathrm{~m}$. What will be the height of receiving antenna, if the maximum distance between them for satisfactory communication in line-of-sight (LOS) mode is $40 \mathrm{~km}$ ? (The earth radius is $6400 \mathrm{~km}$.)

Given, height of transmitting antenna $h_t=20 \mathrm{~m}$, maximum line of sight (LOS) distance between receiving antenna and transmitting antenna $=40 \mathrm{~km}$ and radius of Earth, $R=6400 \mathrm{~km}$. The maximum line of sight distance,
$\begin{aligned} \\ & d_m=\sqrt{2 R h_T}+\sqrt{2 R h_R} \\ \\ & \Rightarrow 40 \times 10^3=\sqrt{2 \times 6.4 \times 10^6 \times 20}+ \\ \\ & \sqrt{2 \times 6.4 \times 10^6 \times x} \\ \\ & \Rightarrow \sqrt{2 \times 6.4 \times 10^6 x}=24000 \\ \\ & \Rightarrow x=45 \mathrm{~m} \\ \end{aligned}$
Hence, the correct option is (4).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A message signal is used to modulate a carrier frequency. If the peak voltages of message signal and carrier signals are increased by $0.1 \%$ and $0.3 \%$ respectively, then the percentage change in modulation index is
questions.solution:
(d) We know that, the modulation index is given by
$\mu=\frac{A_m}{A_c}$
where, $A_m=$ maximum amplitude of message signal and $A_c=$ maximum amplitude of carrier-signal.
Given, $A_m$ and $A_c$ are increased by $0.1 \%$ and $0.3 \%$, then the modulation index becomes,
$\begin{aligned} \\ \mu_1 & =\frac{A_m+0.001 A_m}{A_c+0.003 A_c} \\ \\ & =\frac{1001 A_m}{1003 A_c}=\frac{1001}{1003} \mu \\ \\ \Rightarrow \quad \frac{\mu_1}{\mu} & =\frac{1001}{1003} \\ \end{aligned}$
[From Eq. (i)]
The percentage change in modulation index,
$\begin{aligned} \\ & =\frac{\mu_1-\mu}{\mu} \times 100 \\ \\ & =\frac{1001-1003}{1003} \times 100 \\ \end{aligned}$
$=-\frac{2}{1003} \times 100 \simeq-0.2 \%$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A person tries to broadcast with the same antenna both the signals at $10^7 \mathrm{~Hz}$ and $10^6 \mathrm{~Hz}$. If the receiver at some distance has to receive an equal strength for both the frequencies, then the broadcaster has to approximately increase the signal strength at $10^6 \mathrm{~Hz}$ to $10^7 \mathrm{~Hz}$ by
questions.solution:
Power of signal radiated by an antenna $P \propto \frac{1}{\lambda^2}$, where, $\lambda=$ wavelength of signal or $P \propto v^2$, where, $v=$ frequency so
$\frac{P_1}{P_2}=\frac{v_1^2}{v_2^2}$
Given, $v_1=10^7 \mathrm{~Hz}, \mathrm{v}_2=10^6 \mathrm{~Hz}$
$\begin{aligned} \\ \frac{P_1}{P_2} & =\left(\frac{10^7}{10^6}\right)^2=100 \\ \\ \Rightarrow \quad P_1 & =100 P_2 \\ \end{aligned}$
Power of frequency $10^7$ is 100 times greater than $10^6$. So, signal strength of frequency $10^6 \mathrm{~Hz}$ need to be increased by 100 times for equal strength at some distance.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An amplitude modulated signal consists of a message signal of frequency $1 \mathrm{KHz}$ and peak voltage of $5 \mathrm{~V}$, modulating a carrier frequency of $1 \mathrm{MHz}$ and peak voltage of $15 \mathrm{~V}$. The correct description of this signal is
questions.solution:
Given,
Frequency of message signal $\left(f_m\right)=1 \mathrm{KHz}$
$=1 \times 10^3 \mathrm{~Hz}$
Peak voltage of message signal $\left(E_m\right)=5 \mathrm{~V}$
Carrier frequency $\left\langle f_c\right\rangle=1 \mathrm{MHz}=1 \times 10^6 \mathrm{~Hz}$
Peak voltage of carrier $\left(E_c\right)=15 \mathrm{~V}$
We know that, The equation of amplitude modulated wave is given by
$\begin{aligned} \\ e(t) & =E_c\left[1+\frac{E_m}{E_o} \sin \omega_m t\right] \sin \omega_c t \\ \\ & =E_c\left[1+\frac{E_m}{E_o} \sin \left(2 \pi f_m\right)\right] \sin 2 \pi f_c t \\ \\ & =15\left[1+\frac{5}{15} \sin \left(2 \pi \times 10^3\right)\right] \sin 2 \pi \times 10^6 t \\ \\ & =15\left[1+\frac{1}{3} \sin \left(2 \pi 10^3 t\right)\right] \sin \left(2 \pi 10^6 t\right) \\ \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A transmitting and receiving antenna have height of $d$ metres each. The maximum distance between them for satisfactory communication in Line-of-Sight mode (LOS) is $2 d$ kilometers. If the radius of earth is $6400 \mathrm{~km}$, then the value of $d$ is
questions.solution:
For satisfactory communication, maximum distance
$d_{\max }=\sqrt{2 R h_1}+\sqrt{2 R h_2}$
Given, $\quad d_{\max }=2 d(\mathrm{~km})$ and $h_1=h_2=d(\mathrm{~m})$
From Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get
$2 d=\sqrt{2 R h_1}+\sqrt{2 R h_2}$
Substituting values in Eq. (iii) we get
$\begin{gathered} \\ 2 d \times 1000=2 \sqrt{2 \times 6400 \times 1000 \times d} \\ \\ \Rightarrow \quad(1000)^2 d^2=2 \times 6400 \times 1000 \times d \\ \\ d=\frac{2 \times 6400 \times 1000}{1000 \times 1000} \mathrm{~m}=12.8 \mathrm{~m} \\ \end{gathered}$

questions.q:
A message signal is super-imposed with a carrier signal. The resulting modulating signal $C_m(t)$ is given by
$C_m(t)=A_1 \sin \left(\omega_1 t\right)+A_2 \sin \left(\omega_2 t\right)-A_2 \sin \left(\omega_3 t\right) \text {, }$
where $\omega_2 \lt  \omega_1 \lt  \omega_3$. The modulation index and the angular frequency fo the message signal respectively, are
questions.solution:
Modulating signal is given as
$C_m(t)=A_1 \sin \left(\omega_1 t\right)+A_2 \sin \left(\omega_2 t\right)-A_3 \sin \left(\omega_3 t\right)\ldots(\mathrm{i})$
where, $\quad \omega_1\gt \omega_2$ and $\omega_3\gt \omega_1$
Standard equation of modulating signal is given as
$C_m(t)=A_c \sin \left(\omega_c t\right)+\frac{\mu A_c}{2} \cos \left(\omega_c-\omega_m\right) t-\frac{\mu A_c}{2}\cos \left(\omega_c+\omega_m\right) t$ ...(ii)
Clearly, $\omega_c\gt \omega_c-\omega_m$ and $\omega_c+\omega_m\gt \omega_c$
Eq. (i) can also be written as,
$C_m(t)=A_1 \sin \left(\omega_1 t\right)+A_2 \cos \left(\frac{\pi}{2}+\omega_2 t\right)-A_3 \cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2}+\omega_3 t\right) \ldots$ (iii)
Comparing Eq. (ii) and Eq. (iii), we get
$A_1=A_c\omega_c=\omega_1\omega_c-\omega_m=\omega_2\ldots(\mathrm{iv})$
and $\quad \omega_c+\omega_m=\omega_3\ldots(\mathrm{v})$
Also, $\quad \frac{\mu A_c}{2}=A_2 \Rightarrow \mu=\frac{2 A_2}{A_1}\ldots(\mathrm{vi})$
Substracting Eq. (iv) from Eq. (v), we have $\omega_3-\omega_2=\left(\omega_c+\omega_m\right)-\left(\omega_c-\omega_m\right)\Rightarrow \quad 2 \omega_m=\omega_3-\omega_2\Rightarrow \quad \omega_m=\frac{\omega_3-\omega_2}{2}\ldots(\mathrm{vii})$
From Eq. (vi) and (vii), option (d) is correct.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A TV transmitting antenna is $128 \mathrm{~m}$, tall. If the receiving antenna is at the ground level, the maximum distance between, them for satisfactory communication in line of sight mode is (radius of the earth $6.4 \times 10^6 \mathrm{~m}$ )
questions.solution:
Height of transmitting antenna $d \approx \sqrt{2 R_e h_T}$
Given
$\begin{aligned} \\ R_e & =6.4 \times 10^6 \mathrm{~m} \\ \\ h_T & =128 \mathrm{~m} \\ \\ d & =? \\ \end{aligned}$
The maximum distance
$\begin{aligned} \\ & d=\sqrt{2 \times 6.4 \times 10^6 \times 128} \\ \\ & d=\sqrt{128 \times 10^5 \times 128} \\ \\ & d=\frac{128 \times 10^2 \sqrt{10}}{\sqrt{10}} \times \sqrt{10} \\ \\ & d=\frac{128 \times 10^3}{\sqrt{10}} \mathrm{~m}=\frac{128}{\sqrt{10}} \mathrm{~km} \\ \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: For a television network, $5 \times 10^5$ channels are granted. If the central frequency of the microwave link is $25 \mathrm{GHz}$ and the alloted bandwidth for each channel is $2 \mathrm{kHz}$, then how much percentage of the link is used for the network?
questions.solution:
Let $x \%$ of link is used for network.
Given, central frequency $=25 \mathrm{GHz}$
$=25 \times 10^9 \mathrm{~Hz}$
Bandwidth of channels $=x \%$ of $25 \mathrm{GHz}$
$=\frac{x}{100} \times 25 \times 10^9=25 x \times 10^7$
Number of channel
$\begin{aligned} \\ & =\frac{\text { Total Bandwidth }}{\text { Bandwidth needed per channel }} \\ \\ 5 \times 10^5 & =\frac{25 \times \times 10^7}{2 \times 10^3} \\ \\ 10 \times 10^8 & =25 \times \times 10^7 \\ \\ 25 x & =100 \\ \\ \Rightarrow \quad x & =4 \% \\ \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: For an amplitude modulated wave, the maximum and minimum amplitudes are found to be 10 V and 2 V respectively. Then the modulation index is
questions.solution:
For amplitude modulated wave,
$A_{\max }=10 \mathrm{~V}, \mathrm{~A}_{\min }=2 \mathrm{~V}\therefore$ Modulation index,
$\mu=\frac{\mathrm{A}_{\max }-\mathrm{A}_{\min }}{\mathrm{A}_{\max }+\mathrm{A}_{\min }}=\frac{10-2}{10+2}=\frac{2}{3}$
